big_case_rationale: Nationwide rule for what pipeline condemnors must pay landowners under the Natural Gas Act — consequential for energy infrastructure and property owners across at least five circuits, but a technical choice-of-law question with modest general-public salience.

semantic_claims.proposition: The majority will hold that federal law, not borrowed state law, supplies the measure of compensation in private condemnations under 15 U.S.C. §717f(h): because PennEast v. New Jersey characterized §717f(h) as a delegation of the federal government's own eminent-domain power, the Fifth Amendment standard of the United States v. Miller line governs, and — relying on United States v. Bodcaw Co. (attorney's fees are not part of constitutional just compensation) and the American Rule of Alyeska Pipeline (no fee award in a federal cause of action absent express congressional authorization) — it will reject the Kimbell Foods state-law-borrowing analysis of the Third, Fifth, Sixth, and Eleventh Circuits, holding that the NGA's silence does not incorporate state fee-shifting statutes such as North Dakota's.

The majority's stated ground will be categorical rather than fact-bound: a uniform nationwide rule that federal law governs the measure of compensation in every private condemnation under §717f(h), abrogating the state-law-borrowing rule followed in the Third, Fifth, Sixth, and Eleventh Circuits — not a narrow holding confined to North Dakota's discretionary fee-shifting statute or to attorney's fees alone.
